title: Pings in the Last Three Seconds
statement:
A server receives pings, each stamped with a time t in milliseconds. After each ping, report how busy the server has been lately.

  • PingWindow() starts with no pings.
  • ping(t) records a ping at time t and returns how many pings, including this one, arrived in the closed range [t − 3000, t].

Every call uses a strictly larger t than the call before it.

Tests are a list of operations; the first one creates the counter. The output has one entry per operation (null for the constructor).

examples.why: At 3005 the window is [5, 3005], and the ping at 5 sits exactly on its edge, so it counts. At 5001 the window starts at 2001, so the ping at 2000 misses it by one millisecond.
The gap from 100 to 5000 is longer than 3 seconds, so the old ping is gone.

constraints: t strictly increases from call to call
hints: Times only go up. Once a ping is too old for one call, can it ever count again?
Old pings always leave from the oldest end, and new pings join at the newest end. That is a queue.
Push t, then drop pings from the front while they are smaller than t − 3000. The queue length is the answer.

explain.intuition:
Because t only grows, the window [t − 3000, t] only slides to the right. A ping that falls off its left edge is gone for good. So keep the pings that are still inside the window in a queue: the newest joins at the back, the oldest leaves from the front. After the clean-up, the queue length is the count.

Each ping enters once and leaves once, so the total work is O(n) across all calls. It is the same sliding window as a rate limiter that allows N requests per few seconds.
steps: Keep a queue of times (an array plus a head index works well in JavaScript).
While the front time is less than t − 3000, remove it.
Return the number of times left in the queue.
pitfalls: Dropping pings at exactly t − 3000. The range is closed, so that ping still counts, as the first example shows.
Using Array.shift() in JavaScript. It moves every element and makes each call O(n). Move a head index instead.
Recounting all stored pings on every call: O(n) per call and O(n²) overall.

solutions.title: Store everything, count every time
solutions.idea: Keep every ping and count those inside the window on each call.

solutions.title: Queue of recent pings
solutions.idea: Add the new ping at the back and drop expired pings from the front. What is left is exactly the window.

solutions.title: Binary search on the sorted times
solutions.idea: The times are already sorted, so find the first one ≥ t − 3000 with binary search. Useful when you must keep all history anyway.

followups: Pings can now share the same millisecond and millions arrive per second. How do you keep memory bounded? (Hint: buckets per millisecond.)
Answer the count for an arbitrary past window, not just the latest one. Which solution above already supports that?
